result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.is_minimal_d_separator()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Check if a set d-separates two others and no proper subset does. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.is_minimal_d_separator()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Check if a set d-separates two others and no proper subset does. title: >- [Graph.is_minimal_d_separator()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Check if a set d-separates two others and no proper subset does. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set d-separates two others and no proper subset does. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L57909-L57988){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.is_minimal_d_separator( x, y, z, included=None, restricted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is minimal d-separator](../assets/graphs/is-minimal-d-separator.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The chain A to B to C to D, with A in teal and D in violet. Left: z = [B] (outlined) blocks the chain, and dropping B would open it, so is_minimal_d_separator returns True. Right: z = [B, C] also separates A from D, but C (accent) is not needed, since B alone already blocks the chain, so the set is not minimal and the call returns False." width="100%"} A d-separator `z` of `x` and `y` (see `is_d_separator()`) is *minimal* when removing any node from it breaks the separation. Minimal separators are the smallest sets of variables that must be measured to make `x` and `y` conditionally independent, which keeps causal adjustment sets lean. With `included=`, nodes that must be in the separator are fixed and only the other nodes have to be needed; with `restricted=`, the separator may only use the given nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name} : Nodes, or lists of nodes, as IDs or labels. [y]{.doc-parameter-name} : Nodes, or lists of nodes, as IDs or labels. [z]{.doc-parameter-name} : The candidate separator (a node or a list). [included]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional nodes that are required to be in `z` (and are exempt from minimality). [restricted]{.doc-parameter-name}[=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op}[None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional nodes that `z` must be drawn from (default: all nodes). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if `z` is a minimal d-separator of `x` and `y` under the constraints. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not a directed acyclic graph, a node does not exist, the sets are not disjoint, `included` is not part of `z`, or `z` is not part of `restricted`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The test of van der Zander, Liśkiewicz and Textor (2019), as in NetworkX: `z` must lie within the ancestors of `x`, `y` and `included`, must not let `x` reach `y`, and every node of `z` outside `included` must be reachable (by open paths given `z`) from both `x` and `y`, so dropping it would open a path. It runs in $O(V + E)$ time. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In the chain A -> B -> C -> D, either B or C alone separates A from D, so both are minimal, while {B, C} separates but is not minimal: ::: {#cda32326 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ( g.is_minimal_d_separator("A", "D", ["B"]), g.is_minimal_d_separator("A", "D", ["B", "C"]), g.is_d_separator("A", "D", ["B", "C"]), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False, True) ``` ::: :::
